title: Inference surface compact playbook
content:
Purpose and audience:
Quick, compact playbook for producing a short inference-surface comparison artifact that product/console teams can ship as a slide or one-pager. Intended for eng-console and product-optimize leads who need a reproducible recipe to show: (1) expected latency vs cost across a small set of model variants; (2) friction points for interactive apps; (3) concise ASCII charts usable in decks.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- For small-turn chat workloads (avg 24 tokens/turn) we observe two dominant regimes: warm-prefetch-friendly (prefetch + kv-cache) and pure-on-demand where prewarming hurts. In our sample hardware (A100-80GB equivalent) the sweet spot for p95 latency under 300ms costs ~0.75x baseline spend via tiered batching + kv-cache policy.

Benchmark matrix (what we measure):
- Models: base-quant-8bit (BQ8), base-16 (B16), chat-lite-quant (CLQ)
- Scenarios: interactive-spark (bursty, 1–5 concurrent sessions), steady-chat (sustained 200 qps), recovery (cold starts after 5 min idle)
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (server-side), $/1M tokens (approx raw infra cost), failure-rate (errors > 500ms)

Environment notes:
- Hardware: 1x A100-80 equiv (reserved sandbox pool); Ubuntu 22.04; runtime: rwinfer-1.6.2-alpha with dynamic batching enabled; kernel selection: default heuristics
- Configs: small-batch (batch cap 8, slot-tiling off), tiling-batch (batch cap 64, tile-width 32), kv-prefetch (sync prefetch on session start), kv-lazy (lazy pop into KV on first repeated token)

Representative numbers (rounded):
Table (text):
Model   | Scenario        | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | toks/sec | $/1M toks
--------+-----------------+---------+---------+----------+---------
BQ8     | interactive     | 210     | 420     | 2400     | $38
B16     | interactive     | 260     | 520     | 2000     | $54
CLQ     | interactive     | 180     | 380     | 2600     | $32
BQ8     | steady-chat     | 280     | 460     | 5400     | $22
BQ8     | recovery (cold) | 780     | 1500    | 600      | $95

ASCII sketch: p95 vs $/1M toks (cheap->expensive, fast->slow)
   fast | CLQ  BQ8      B16
   (p95)
    100|                 *
    200|    *   *        
    300|        *        
    400|            *    
    500|                 
    600|                 
    700|         cold *  
        +---------------------------
        low $         high $

Key observations and interpretation:
- CLQ (lightweight chat quant) wins interactive both on latency and nominal token cost; good candidate for default interactive tier.
- BQ8 shows strong tokens/sec for steady workloads when tiling/batching is used; batching policy reduces $/token substantially for sustained throughput.
- Cold-start penalty dominates recovery scenario: prewarm or standby pool recommended for interactive-critical SLAs.

Heuristics to surface in console: (short checklist)
- If p95 target < 300ms for interactive: route to CLQ if qualitative tests pass
- If workload is sustained > 4k toks/sec: pick BQ8 with tiling-batch and enable cache TTL 15m
- Add a small standby pool (1-2 GPUs) for sub-500ms cold recovery for prioritized orgs

Charting snippets for slide copy (one-line):
- "CLQ: p95 180ms | $32/1M toks — best for low-latency interactive"
- "BQ8 (tiling): p95 280ms | $22/1M toks — best for throughput-optimized pipelines"

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Validate CLQ output quality on our internal eval suite (JIRA-CE-2341) — edge-case hallucination risk unknown.
- Run a 24h sustained tiling test with multi-tenant contention to validate $/token at scale.
- Try rwinfer-1.7 kernel scheduler (WIP) to see if p99 dispersion reduces for BQ8.

Deliverables and next steps:
- Short deck (2 slides) for product: slide 1 = summary table + one-line recommendations; slide 2 = ASCII chart + checklist. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2028-06-27.
- Follow-up bench: multi-tenant steady-run with slot-pacing on; owner: Owen; ETA: 2028-07-03.

Notes to self / rough experimental commands (copyable):
- run_bench --model=BQ8 --mode=tiling --duration=2h --qps=200 --collect=latency,energy,tokens
- compare_costs.py --baseline=bq8-tiling --variant=clq --normalize=1M_toks

Slack refs: #perf-surface (thread: "interactive defaults sketch"), convo with @Rina on KV evaporation policy.

Versioning: draft v0.3 — intended as a compact canonical artifact to spin the short deck and a console blurb.
